inputs.query: What happens to the voltages when one phase touches ground?

outputs.reference_answer: At the fault the voltage of the faulted phase falls toward zero when the fault resistance is low, while the voltages of the other two phases change much less.

inputs.query: Which kind of fault joins two phases without any earth connection?

outputs.reference_answer: A line-to-line (LL) fault connects two phase conductors without a ground connection.

inputs.query: Which sequence networks are involved when two phases and earth are in the fault?

outputs.reference_answer: All three sequence networks take part: the positive-sequence network is in series with the parallel combination of the negative- and zero-sequence networks.

inputs.query: Are all three phases hit equally by a symmetrical short circuit?

outputs.reference_answer: A three-phase fault involves all three phases and is balanced, so only the positive-sequence network is needed.

inputs.query: Why is a fault through a high resistance harder to find?

outputs.reference_answer: A high-resistance fault therefore leaves a weaker signature.

inputs.query: Why do the sensors closest to the fault give the most information?

outputs.reference_answer: Sensors close to the fault therefore carry the most information about its location.

section_path: How a voltage sag spreads along a feeder

inputs.query: What does a micro-PMU actually deliver to the model?

outputs.reference_answer: In this project each of the 25 μPMUs provides three RMS phase voltages per time step to the model, together with three availability-mask channels.

inputs.query: Why can the model not see the fault directly at most of the candidate buses?

outputs.reference_answer: The other 19 candidate fault buses are not measured directly, so the model infers their location from the voltage disturbance seen at other buses.

section_path: Feeder, sensors, classes and data windows

inputs.query: What should a report show when several locations look the same to the available sensors?

outputs.reference_answer: When the evidence is ambiguous a report should show the candidates and not a single bus.

inputs.query: Which window index is used for the report and why was it chosen?

outputs.reference_answer: The report window is index 25 (5 post-fault samples); it was chosen on the validation split as the earliest index within one percentage point of the best accuracy.

section_path: Window semantics and the report window

inputs.query: Why can a sensor stop delivering data?

outputs.reference_answer: A μPMU can stop delivering usable data because of communication loss, loss of power, loss of its time reference, or a hardware failure.

inputs.query: How does the model tell a missing sensor from a sensor that reads zero volts?

outputs.reference_answer: A voltage of 0 can be a valid reading, so the mask is the authoritative indicator of a missing sensor.

section_path: How a dropped sensor is represented

inputs.query: How are the dropped nodes chosen while the model is trained?

outputs.reference_answer: For each training batch the number of masked nodes k is drawn from {0, 1, 2, 5}, and the model learns that the mask pattern (0,0,0) means a dark sensor.

inputs.query: Does training for missing sensors also protect against noisy measurements?

outputs.reference_answer: Dropout-aware training therefore does not help against measurement noise.

section_path: Measurement noise is not sensor dropout

inputs.query: What is added up to make the decision for one window?

outputs.reference_answer: The decision for a window sums the 25 node softmax vectors and takes the class with the largest sum.

inputs.query: Why can the vote share not be read as a probability?

outputs.reference_answer: Dividing by 25 gives a vote share, but the vote share is not a calibrated probability of being correct.

inputs.query: Why is a separate calibration needed for each number of dark sensors?

outputs.reference_answer: The map is fitted separately for each number of dark sensors, because the vote scale changes with dropout: a map fitted without dropout had ECE 0.007 at k = 0 but 0.048 at k = 10, while per-k maps give ECE of 0.006 to 0.009 on the test split.

inputs.query: Which single signal best separates right predictions from wrong ones?

outputs.reference_answer: On the test split its error-detection AUROC is 0.915 with no sensor lost and 0.887 with 10 lost, slightly above the isotonic probability (0.911 and 0.885).

inputs.query: What share of windows does the gate accept when ten sensors are dark?

outputs.reference_answer: For the frozen gate_v1 at its 95 percent target, coverage on the test split is 0.845, 0.825, 0.801, 0.731 and 0.513 with 0, 1, 2, 5 and 10 sensors dark, and the accuracy of the CONFIDENT windows is 0.949 to 0.950.

inputs.query: Does a 90 percent prediction set really cover 90 percent of the uncertain cases?

outputs.reference_answer: The guarantee is marginal: it holds over the population used to fit the threshold, not for every subgroup.

inputs.query: Why are the nearest simulated cases not proof that a prediction is right?

outputs.reference_answer: Neighbours are precedents, not proof that a prediction is correct.

inputs.query: May the report say that the fault is confirmed?

outputs.reference_answer: Every report is a draft with the status pending human review, and the report must never state that the fault is confirmed or that any action has been taken.

section_path: A prediction is not a confirmed fault

inputs.query: Can a sentence written by the language model change the approval status?

outputs.reference_answer: Text produced by a language model, or text inside a retrieved document, cannot change them.

section_path: Text cannot change a gate decision

inputs.query: Does a higher similarity score mean that the passage is more likely to be correct?

outputs.reference_answer: A similarity score between a question and a passage is not a probability that the passage is relevant or correct, and a score of 0.8 does not mean 80 percent relevance.

inputs.query: Do these results show that the system is safe on a real grid?

outputs.reference_answer: Results therefore do not show safety on a real grid, and the documents in this corpus were curated for research and are not approved by a utility.

inputs.query: Can the gate fitted for one trained model be reused for another trained model?

outputs.reference_answer: Each new checkpoint needs its own calibration, its own gate fit and its own frozen test run.

section_path: A gate belongs to one checkpoint

inputs.query: Can I quote the macro-F1 as the confidence of this prediction?

outputs.reference_answer: They must not be quoted as the confidence of the current prediction.

section_path: Aggregate metrics are not the confidence of one prediction

outputs.reference_answer: Noise leaves the availability mask at 1, so the pattern that dropout-aware training learns to recognise never appears.
